column6: The commentary recalls Joseph disappearing into the pit before reaching a caravan; Genesis tells the same scene, with the pit empty of water.

column5: pulled from the pit into the traders' route
column6: The commentary says Joseph's disappearance in the pit leads to the road and travelers; Genesis has passing traders draw him up and carry him into their journey.

column5: Joseph interprets his journey as being sent ahead
column6: The commentary reads the pit's disappearance as a route with an eventual destination; Joseph later says God sent him ahead to preserve life, interpreting that route as purposeful.

column5: Joseph sold, yet God was with him
column6: The commentary's Joseph vanishes from his brothers and passes into travelers' hands; Stephen retells the sale to Egypt while stressing that God was with Joseph.

column5: pit containing no water but danger
column6: The commentary treats the pit as Joseph's hiding place before the caravan route; Genesis Rabbah reads its emptiness of water as leaving snakes and scorpions, heightening the apparent finality from which Joseph emerges.

column5: God calls and the dead answer
column6: The commentary connects disappearance in earth with eventual meeting; Job imagines God calling and the dead answering, giving the hoped-for return a personal encounter.

column5: the dead hear and come out
column6: The commentary's dead are hidden in earth; Jesus says all in the tombs will hear his voice.

column5: earth gives up those asleep in it
column6: The commentary's dalal includes burial in earth; 4 Ezra pictures the earth restoring those who sleep in it at the judgment.

column5: idol makers and witnesses are nothing
column6: The commentary says fabricated objects vanish at the gathering; Isaiah calls the makers of idols nothing and their witnesses unable to see or know.

column5: idol worshippers cannot see or understand
column6: The commentary depicts fabricated objects disappearing from their adherents; Isaiah says the idol-makers' eyes are shut and their hearts cannot understand.

column5: the dead stand before the throne
column6: The commentary says no one is absent from the Day of Judgment; Revelation pictures the dead, great and small, standing before the throne as books are opened.

column5: all stand before God's judgment seat
column6: The commentary denies anyone can be absent from judgment; Paul says all will stand before God's judgment seat.
